bounded_statement: The selected result in results/report.md is a Mann-Whitney U test computed on two arms taken from columns `a` and `b` of the same 12 rows, so each of the 12 distinct `k1`,`k2` source items enters this two-independent-samples rank procedure twice; the reported statistic 60.5 lies on the U scale for n1=n2=12, i.e. 24 observations treated as mutually independent when only 12 authorized independent units exist.

counterevidence_considered.description: No ordered `k1`,`k2` pair repeats across rows, so the issue is not instantiated as row-level duplication of a unit; it arises from the same unit supplying one entry to each arm.
Unlike a t-test result, the reported output contains no degrees-of-freedom field, so the effective sample size is inferred from the U statistic's scale rather than stated outright in the report.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: report contains only statistic and pvalue

evidence.description: task.md designates the ordered `k1`,`k2` pair as the source item, making `a` and `b` on a row two measurements of one unit.

source_refs.quoted_text: Apply the named procedure to the complete staged row sequence. Treat each distinct ordered `k1`,`k2` pair as one source item; rows carrying the same ordered pair originate from the same source item.

evidence.description: Both comparison arms are comprehensions over the same `rows` list, one per column, so each unit contributes exactly one entry to each arm.

left = [float(row["a"]) for row in rows]
right = [float(row["b"]) for row in rows]

evidence.description: The procedure applied is the two-independent-samples Mann-Whitney U test, which assumes independence both within and between the two arms.
The staged file supplies 12 rows / 12 source items, each carrying both an `a` and a `b` measurement, for 24 measurements fed to the test.
The selected result is reported on the between-groups U scale (maximum 12*12=144, midpoint 72), confirming the arms were compared as two independent groups of 12 rather than as 12 matched units.
evidence.observed_value: statistic=60.5 on the U scale for n1=n2=12

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted three refutations. (1) Row-level duplication: I checked all 12 ordered `k1`,`k2` pairs and found them distinct, and the workflow applies no grouping or aggregation before testing, so under a reading of the class limited to a unit spanning multiple rows the finding would fail; the mechanism here is instead one unit supplying one entry to each arm. (2) Independent arms: if `a` and `b` came from different source items the test would be appropriate, but task.md ties the source item to the ordered pair carried by the row that holds both values, so the arms are matched on the same 12 units. (3) Unit-respecting output: I checked whether the reported number could have come from a within-unit rank procedure; a signed-rank statistic on 12 pairs is bounded by 78 and `mannwhitneyu` computes only the between-groups U (bounded by 144, here 60.5 with a half-integer from ties across arms), and the call site passes the two raw column lists, so the reported value can only be the independent-groups statistic over 24 entries. The verdict survives; the residual uncertainty is the absence of an explicit df field, which the U scale compensates for.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py derives `left` and `right` from two columns of the identical row list and passes them to `scipy.stats.mannwhitneyu`, whose null distribution is the distribution of ranks under mutual independence of all entries in both arms. Because task.md designates each ordered `k1`,`k2` pair as one source item, `a` and `b` on a row are two measurements of the same unit; the workflow discards that within-unit matching instead of using a within-unit rank procedure or reducing each unit to one entry.
